ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in the Cartesian coordinate system, the vertex $A$ of $\square OABC$ lies on the inverse proportional function $y=\frac{1}{x}$, the vertex $B$ lies on the inverse proportional function $y=\frac{5}{x}$, and point $C$ is located on the positive half of the $x$-axis. What is the area of $\square OABC$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure, draw perpendiculars from points A and B to the x-axis, with the feet of the perpendiculars being M and N, respectively, and connect OB. \\
Since quadrilateral ABCO is a parallelogram, \\
it follows that $OA=BC$ and $AB\parallel OC$, \\
which means $AM=BN$, \\
In $\triangle AMO$ and $\triangle BNC$ right-angled triangles, \\
since $OA=CB$ and $AM=BN$, \\
it leads to $\triangle AMO \cong \triangle BNC$ (HL criterion), \\
Also, since point A lies on the inverse proportion function $y=\frac{1}{x}$, \\
it implies $Area_{\triangle AOM}=\frac{1}{2}\times 1=\frac{1}{2}=Area_{\triangle BNC}$, \\
Since point B lies on the inverse proportion function $y=\frac{5}{x}$, \\
it implies $Area_{\triangle BON}=\frac{1}{2}\times 5=\frac{5}{2}$, \\
Therefore, $Area_{\triangle OBC}=Area_{\triangle BON}-Area_{\triangle BNC}=\frac{5}{2}-\frac{1}{2}=2=\frac{1}{2}Area_{\square ABCO}$, \\
Thus, $Area_{\square ABCO}=\boxed{4}$.

method.method_draft: Use an auxiliary-line area decomposition. From the image first note that OABC is a parallelogram: O is the origin, OC lies on the positive x-axis, AB is horizontal and parallel to OC, and OA is parallel to BC. Drop perpendiculars from A and B to the x-axis, with feet M and N, and draw OB. From the text use A on y=1/x and B on y=5/x. For any point (x,y) on y=k/x in the first quadrant, the rectangle to the axes has area xy=k, so the right triangle with the origin and the x-axis foot has area k/2. Thus area(△AOM)=1/2 and area(△BON)=5/2. Since OABC is a parallelogram with AB horizontal, the right triangles △AOM and △BNC are congruent, so area(△BNC)=1/2. Then area(△OBC)=area(△BON)-area(△BNC)=2, and diagonal OB halves the parallelogram, giving area(OABC)=4.
method.CoT_raw:
先描述图像：图中是直角坐标系，O 在原点，C 位于 x 轴正半轴上。四边形 OABC 画成一个平行四边形：OC 沿 x 轴水平向右，AB 也是水平线段并与 OC 平行，OA 与 BC 是两条斜边且彼此平行。点 A 在较低的反比例曲线 y=1/x 上，点 B 在较高的反比例曲线 y=5/x 上。

再推理：按辅助线面积分解，分别从 A、B 向 x 轴作垂线，垂足为 M、N，并连接 OB。对第一象限内反比例函数 y=k/x 上的点 (x,y)，有 xy=k，所以由该点、原点和它在 x 轴上的垂足组成的直角三角形面积为 xy/2=k/2。

因为 A 在 y=1/x 上，所以 Area(△AOM)=1/2。因为 B 在 y=5/x 上，所以 Area(△BON)=5/2。

又因为 OABC 是平行四边形，OA=BC，且 AB∥OC，所以 A、B 到 x 轴的高度相同，即 AM=BN。△AOM 和 △BNC 都是直角三角形，斜边 OA=BC，且一条直角边 AM=BN，因此 △AOM≅△BNC，所以 Area(△BNC)=Area(△AOM)=1/2。

因此 Area(△OBC)=Area(△BON)-Area(△BNC)=5/2-1/2=2。对平行四边形 OABC，连接对角线 OB 会把它分成两个面积相等的三角形，所以 Area(OABC)=2×Area(△OBC)=2×2=4。

raw_record.original_question: In the Cartesian coordinate system, as shown in the figure, vertex $A$ of $\square OABC$ lies on the inverse proportional function $y=\frac{1}{x}$, vertex $B$ lies on the inverse proportional function $y=\frac{5}{x}$, and point $C$ is on the positive half of the $x$-axis. What is the area of $\square OABC$?
raw_record.answer: Solution: Draw perpendiculars from points $A$ and $B$ to the $x$-axis, with feet $M$ and $N$, and connect $OB$. Since quadrilateral $ABCO$ is a parallelogram, $OA=BC$ and $AB\parallel OC$, so $AM=BN$. In right triangles $\triangle AMO$ and $\triangle BNC$, with $OA=CB$ and $AM=BN$, we get $\triangle AMO \cong \triangle BNC$ (HL). Since $A$ lies on $y=\frac{1}{x}$, $Area_{\triangle AOM}=\frac{1}{2}\times 1=\frac{1}{2}=Area_{\triangle BNC}$. Since $B$ lies on $y=\frac{5}{x}$, $Area_{\triangle BON}=\frac{1}{2}\times 5=\frac{5}{2}$. Therefore, $Area_{\triangle OBC}=Area_{\triangle BON}-Area_{\triangle BNC}=\frac{5}{2}-\frac{1}{2}=2=\frac{1}{2}Area_{\square ABCO}$. Thus, $Area_{\square ABCO}=\boxed{4}$.
raw_record.final_cot:
First describe the image: In the figure is a rectangular coordinate system, O is at the origin, and C is located on the positive half-axis of the x-axis. Quadrilateral OABC is drawn as a parallelogram: OC goes horizontally to the right along the x-axis, AB is also a horizontal line segment and is parallel to OC, and OA and BC are two oblique sides and are parallel to each other. Point A is on the lower inverse proportional curve y=1/x, and point B is on the higher inverse proportional curve y=5/x.

Then reason: According to the auxiliary-line area decomposition, draw perpendiculars from A and B respectively to the x-axis, with feet M and N, and connect OB. For a point (x,y) on the inverse proportional function y=k/x in the first quadrant, xy=k, so the area of the right triangle formed by this point, the origin, and its foot on the x-axis is xy/2=k/2.

Because A is on y=1/x, Area(△AOM)=1/2. Because B is on y=5/x, Area(△BON)=5/2.

Also because OABC is a parallelogram, OA=BC, and AB∥OC, so the heights from A and B to the x-axis are the same, that is, AM=BN. △AOM and △BNC are both right triangles, the hypotenuse OA=BC, and one right-angle side AM=BN, therefore △AOM≅△BNC, so Area(△BNC)=Area(△AOM)=1/2.

Therefore Area(△OBC)=Area(△BON)-Area(△BNC)=5/2-1/2=2. For parallelogram OABC, connecting diagonal OB will divide it into two triangles of equal area, so Area(OABC)=2×Area(△OBC)=2×2=4.
